about: A-One Steels is a backward-integrated steel manufacturer based in southern India, making sponge iron, MS billets, TMT bars, HR/CR coils, pipes, met coke and ferro alloys. It runs six plants across Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh with aggregate installed capacity of 17,33,100 MTPA. It sells through 32 distributors, direct retail dealers and institutional customers, with about 83% of power from renewable and non-captive sources.

objects.purpose: Pre-payment or partial re-payment of certain outstanding borrowings

promoters.background: First-generation promoters who set up the business; the three promoters are also the Promoter Selling Shareholders in the Rs 50 crore offer for sale.

concentration.note: Top 10 customers were 27.90% of FY26 revenue from operations (top 5: 19.41%, largest: 5.33%). Karnataka contributed 54.86% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: Past ROC penalties on the company, directors and promoters (FY21-FY25), a SEBI penalty of Rs 16 lakh (2019, closed), a pending Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission matter on renewable purchase obligations, pollution board notices at several plants, and a Koppal subsidiary closure order stayed by the Karnataka High Court. Contingent liabilities include income tax matters of Rs 30.56 crore and GST matters of Rs 2.00 crore (Mar-26).
strengths: Backward-integrated from sponge iron to billets, TMT bars, coils and pipes, giving control over inputs and quality.
Plants in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh sit near iron ore and within about 450 km of major ports.
FY26 PAT rose to Rs 127.41 crore from Rs 7.71 crore, and EBITDA margin improved to 7.29% from 4.91%.
About 83% of power in FY26 came from renewable and non-captive sources, and TMT bars hold green product certification.
Diversified sales through 32 distributors, 1,246 retail dealers and 57 institutional customers; top 10 customers are 27.90% of revenue.
Debt to equity improved from 2.34 in FY24 to 1.17 in FY26; Rs 250 crore of issue proceeds will repay debt.
Capacity grew from 14,97,100 MTPA (Mar-24) to 17,33,100 MTPA (Mar-26), with a waste heat power plant and ore beneficiation plant under way.
Experienced promoters with a long operating record and a sales and marketing team of 63.

risks.title: Heavy debt and thin margins
risks.detail: Borrowings are about Rs 1,011 crore against net worth of Rs 820 crore (debt/equity 1.17). Finance costs were Rs 53.10 crore in FY26. PAT margin was only 3.06% in FY26 and 0.22% in FY25.

risks.title: Profit swings and may not sustain FY26 level
risks.detail: PAT was Rs 38.91 crore in FY24, fell to Rs 7.71 crore in FY25 and jumped to Rs 127.41 crore in FY26. The FY26 margin may not repeat.

risks.title: Weak operating cash flow and working capital strain
risks.detail: Operating cash flow fell from Rs 325.40 crore in FY24 to Rs 62.80 crore in FY26. Trade receivables rose 51.85% to Rs 664.46 crore in FY26. Working capital days are 53.

risks.title: Steel price cyclicality and raw material cost
risks.detail: Raw materials were 84.05% of FY26 revenue from operations. Steel prices and coking coal, iron ore and scrap costs swing with global and domestic conditions.

risks.title: Geographic concentration in two states
risks.detail: All plants are in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka alone gave 54.86% of FY26 revenue. A local disruption would hurt operations.

risks.title: Regulatory and environmental issues
risks.detail: Pollution board notices (23 across four plants, 2022-2025), a closure order on the Koppal subsidiary stayed by the High Court, and repeated ROC penalties from FY21 to FY25.

risks.title: Promoter loans and guarantees
risks.detail: Promoters have given unsecured loans of Rs 137.67 crore and personal guarantees for company borrowings. Rs 50 crore of the offer is a sale by promoters, so the company gets no money from it.

risks.title: Contingent liabilities and expansion risk
risks.detail: Contingent liabilities include income tax matters of Rs 30.56 crore and Rs 28.92 crore of litigation items. Expansion projects at Koppal depend on approvals, funding and timely commissioning.

notes: Restated consolidated, Rs lakh converted to Rs crore. Revenue is total revenue from operations incl. government grants as in the KPI table; EBITDA excludes other income and exceptional items. Reserves = other equity attributable to owners (derived from garbled balance sheet); net worth as reported in KPI table. Borrowings = non-current + current. Cash and bank = cash plus other bank balances. FY24 EPS 6.56 as reported. Current ratio not reported, left null. Post-IPO P/E not stated. Peer revenue_cr is total income converted from lakh; peer table is garbled so most peer RoNW is null. No stub period.
